name: python-frontend-open-points
body: Open design points for the plan/user (do NOT invent decisions here). (1) Module FQN namespace form — python-package-identity mandates collision-freedom but defers the form. Python package identity is the init-bearing dotted name, which lives in the one shared Module namespace alongside language/package-derived names (Cargo package, npm package, Go module path). A bare dotted name can collide with another language's module (a root package `apg` vs the Rust `apg` module — the ingestor panics on a residual Module FQN collision, SPEC §4), and a flat-stem rule for init-less files can collide two same-stem top-level modules in different directories. The choice — bare dotted FQN, a path-derived absolute-path form like markdown's, or a language-namespaced form — is unresolved and changes the observable FQN, so it needs user input. (2) Cython / .pyx — pinned OUT of the accepted set (python-accept-extensions) because `ty` cannot parse Cython exactly; whether a future Cython frontend or a tree-sitter heuristic arm is wanted is a user call. (3) uv/venv project-context model — `ty` resolves imports against a project environment; how the frontend models that environment (a uv project, a venv, a bare src root; how site-packages is excluded from scanning yet available as a resolution input) governs whether third-party imports resolve to external UnresolvedTargets or are treated as in-project. Deferred. (4) Ruff/ty pin currency — the reference pins ruff tag 0.16.6; whether that tag's ty API still matches current main's needs, and the policy for bumping the pin atomically (as src/rustlib does for rust-analyzer), is a plan-time build decision. (5) Incremental target-set acceptance — the exact target-set/delta interface a frontend receives (per-file vs per-package) and the granularity of the ty/salsa cache under targeted emission are the incremental-content plan's concern (requirements.note.open-design-points); Python's per-module granularity interacts with the package identity model and is not decided here.
